cases.title: Same-domain rename preserves identity and references
cases.initial_state: Object GUID G and current domain SID S have parent A; a group references G.
cases.operation: Rename/move inside the same domain after name/old-parent/new-parent operation rights.
cases.expected: G and S stay stable; only parent/RDN/derived locator changes. Typed DN references resolve G, not a stale text DN.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: A denied move changes neither object, parent edges, indexes, journal, audit nor receipt. Resolve names with schema rules, not SQL collation.

cases.title: Cross-domain move is an explicit SID transition
cases.initial_state: Principal has G and domain-A SID SA; source and destination NC/role authorities are distinct.
cases.operation: A separately qualified cross-domain move is requested.
cases.expected: Preserve object identity as specified by the move protocol, allocate the destination-domain SID under its RID authority and apply only the qualified SID-history/cleanup rules. An applicable SID is not immutable across every domain transition.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Never implement this as an ordinary intradomain rename or allow a caller to choose an arbitrary SID/SID-history. Unsupported migration remains refused.

cases.title: Concurrent originating DN collision
cases.initial_state: Two creates target the same parent and schema-equivalent RDN.
cases.operation: Resolve syntax/matching keys and serialize local uniqueness checks.
cases.expected: At most one local live name key commits; the other originating request receives the specified collision result. This is distinct from replicated naming conflicts.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: The losing request leaves no partial object, state/journal/audit/receipt or reused identity. Escapes and multi-valued RDNs are structural inputs.

cases.title: Schema identity and constraints govern values
cases.initial_state: Class/attribute schema defines syntax, required/allowed attributes, matching rule, links and system-managed fields.
cases.operation: Add/modify an entry under one versioned schema snapshot.
cases.expected: Validate structural/auxiliary class constraints and attribute-specific encodings before commit. Object references use stable identities; preserve display values separately from matching keys.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Reject missing/invalid class/value, unauthorized system-field changes and unknown matching implementations; no generic Unicode casefold or PostgreSQL collation stands in for AD matching.

cases.title: Ordered ACEs and attribute visibility
cases.initial_state: A valid descriptor has an applicable explicit allow of READ_PROPERTY followed by an inherited deny for that same bit; request is only that bit.
cases.operation: Run the Windows ordered access check and operation-specific visibility checks.
cases.expected: The explicit allow satisfies that remaining bit before the later inherited deny. Preserve the specified canonicalization/object-ACE rules; never sort all denies ahead of all allows. Hidden attributes behave absent in both search results and filter evaluation.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: NULL and empty DACLs are distinct; owner/privilege/object/integrity rules are not blanket grants. Wrong attribute/control rights never become a generic object-level allow.

cases.title: Inheritance propagation and protected objects
cases.initial_state: Parent P changes an inheritable ACE; descendant C has a materialized descriptor, while D has a protected DACL.
cases.operation: Commit P and schedule the security-descriptor propagation task.
cases.expected: C is eventually recomputed under class/inheritance flags; D keeps its protected inheritance semantics. AdminSDHolder protection is a separate mechanism. Propagator writes do not create replicated attribute stamps.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Do not claim immediate descendant-wide revocation: the specified background task can span transactions. Show pending propagation; a parent commit acknowledgment is not proof that every descendant already changed.

cases.title: Cycles, token provenance and incomplete membership
cases.initial_state: A links to B, B links to A and a user is reachable through one link; a GC or a traversal budget can be unavailable.
cases.operation: Evaluate a link traversal/computed tokenGroups under the declared operation.
cases.expected: Use visited identities to terminate cycles; follow group scope/security-enabled and primary-group rules. LDAP transitive matching is not PAC/token construction. tokenGroups may be absent without a GC; an explicitly incomplete alternative must be labeled.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Do not reject all cyclic graphs as a universal AD rule, silently truncate authorization expansion or grant from incomplete work. Authenticated ticket/token SID freshness is distinct from current directory membership.

cases.title: Local resource ACL revocation serializes with mutation
cases.initial_state: Actor is authenticated; the target descriptor changes to revoke its requested write before mutation commit.
cases.operation: Acquire the bounded writer/security-version authority and recheck current resource descriptor and operation rights.
cases.expected: Either the write commits before the local descriptor revocation, or it observes the revocation and is denied/retried. Use the verified token context plus current resource policy; do not silently rewrite an already issued PAC.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: A cached grant cannot survive a locally serialized target-ACL revoke. Parent inheritance propagation, old ticket groups and cross-site revocation windows remain explicit separate freshness states.

cases.title: Durable local success and retry boundaries
cases.initial_state: A local mutation has object/name changes, journal, audit intent and actor/request/payload receipt.
cases.operation: Commit them together before acknowledging the local mutation; a response can be lost.
cases.expected: Retry reauthorizes and recovers the same durable receipt, without duplicate effects; changed payload is rejected. Each search/page has its own transaction. Documented post-response background tasks retain their own durable pending state.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: A failed/unknown commit is not success. This is a Babel local atomic contract, not a claim that AD mandates one giant transaction for a whole paged search or all GPO/SYSVOL/background work.

cases.title: Partitioned edits to separate attributes
cases.initial_state: A changes displayName; B changes telephoneNumber for the same G while disconnected.
cases.operation: Deliver the two updates in both orders and include duplicates.
cases.expected: Compare/apply stamps per attribute; both independent winning values survive. Preserve originating stamps, assign receiver-local progress separately.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Object-wide last-writer overwrite or one global SQL sequence must not discard the other attribute.

cases.title: Same-attribute conflict uses attribute stamps
cases.initial_state: A has version 8/time 100; B has version 9/time 90 for the same attribute.
cases.operation: Merge in either delivery order.
cases.expected: B wins by CompareVersions despite its older clock. Equal versions compare timeChanged, then originating invocation GUID; equal comparison leaves the current value. usnOriginating is not an extra conflict tie-breaker.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Do not use wall-clock-only ordering or infer authority from a timestamp; conversion/time precision follows the pinned type.

cases.title: GUID tie-breaking uses little-endian octets
cases.operation: Compare the specified GUID representation.
cases.expected: A compares greater: its first little-endian octet is 01 versus B’s 00. Canonical UUID text order would produce the wrong result.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Do not use database UUID/string ordering without proving the required byte representation.

cases.title: Attribute DWORD version wrap is explicit
cases.initial_state: One version is FFFFFFFF; its next originating update wraps to 00000000. Also compare 00000001 versus 80000001.
cases.operation: Apply the pinned CompareVersions procedure with defined 32-bit arithmetic.
cases.expected: 00000000 is newer than FFFFFFFF in this transition; the explicit half-range case selects 80000001 over 00000001. This is not plain unsigned sorting.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Keep global overflow checks enabled; implement only protocol-defined modular arithmetic explicitly. Do not substitute the link-value comparator or claim arbitrary transitivity across unqualified history gaps.

cases.title: Linked values have lifetime-aware metadata
cases.initial_state: A live/new lifetime has timeCreated 200/version 1; an older lifetime has timeCreated 100/version 300.
cases.operation: Compare link stamps; separately delete/recreate a retained tombstoned link.
cases.expected: Use LinkValueStampCompare, including zero/nonzero-version handling, timeCreated, signed 32-bit version difference, timeChanged and origin GUID. A retained tombstone recreation preserves timeCreated and increments version; a fresh post-GC lifetime differs.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Never apply AttributeStampCompare wholesale to links. timeDeleted maps to the wire presence flag; deletion/recycle cannot create an active orphaned privilege link.

cases.title: Replicated same-name objects do not merge identities
cases.initial_state: Two distinct object GUIDs claim one RDN under one parent. Name timestamps tie; A/B use the GUIDs from R-GUID-ORDER, with different name versions.
cases.operation: Resolve the cross-object name conflict.
cases.expected: Use ResolveNameConflict’s name timestamp and OBJECT GUID rule, not a generic attribute-version/origin-GUID ranking. A keeps the name in this example; preserve B under a conflict RDN containing U+000A + CNF: + B’s dashed GUID.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Keep both principals/identities; never merge by DN. Do not store the documentation’s display placeholder # as the literal conflict separator.

cases.title: Delete/recycle conflict preserves lifecycle invariants
cases.initial_state: A deletes an object while B modifies one attribute or linked membership.
cases.operation: Apply the competing replicated updates and lifecycle repair.
cases.expected: Follow UpdateObject/RemoveObj/RecycleObj and declared optional-feature state; retain required identity/deletion/link metadata and keep deleted/recycled objects out of ordinary active views.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: A retained attribute or delayed backlink cannot silently reactivate a principal or resurrect privileges; undelete has separate authorization/constraints.

cases.title: Receiver progress never outruns applied state
cases.initial_state: A bounded GetNCChanges reply contains objects and link updates plus per-source progress.
cases.operation: Crash before/after applying a page, or lose the reply.
cases.expected: Atomically retain each committed page and its safe local replay/progress checkpoint. Update the source watermark only for applied work; merge the broader UTD/PAS only after all response updates and cycle completion. Replay is idempotent.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Never advance UTD/cursor on an unprocessed/error/partial page. Originating USNs, local USNs, per-source high-watermarks and UTD knowledge are distinct.

cases.title: Restore changes invocation epoch before service
cases.initial_state: A restored copy has old USNs/keys/SYSVOL while peers have advanced.
cases.operation: Start isolated; verify a coherent backup and the qualified restore procedure.
cases.expected: Retain DSA/object identity as specified, establish a fresh invocation ID/USN epoch and reconcile credential/deletion/replica state before service. Keep a versioned local restore checkpoint without inventing a new AD wire field.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: No old USN sequence can continue under its old invocation ID. A VM snapshot alone is not a qualified restore; discard/quarantine stale RID allocations and require native recovery proof later.

cases.title: Expired history prevents unsafe incremental rejoin
cases.initial_state: A replica returns after required deletion/link tombstones have been collected.
cases.operation: Attempt incremental synchronization.
cases.expected: Quarantine and follow the qualified full rebuild/rejoin path when safe incremental knowledge is unavailable; retain explicit stale/unknown status.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: Do not infer absence means a never-created object or silently reintroduce lingering principals/links.

cases.title: RID transfer/seizure and restored allocators
cases.initial_state: One allocator is partitioned while another assumes qualified RID authority.
cases.operation: Consume/transfer/seize only under the specified allocation and recovery policy.
cases.expected: Never allocate duplicate SID ranges or allow an untrusted stale former authority to resume. Verify eligible roles/pools/epoch and rebuild or invalidate stale allocations before serving.
cases.denied_or_interrupted: A PostgreSQL sequence is not the domain RID/FSMO protocol. Exact transfer/seizure implementation and reference drills remain required before native allocation.

boundaries.title: Client to protocol/core
misuse_cases: Malformed/oversized/slow frames exhaust a listener
Unsigned/downgraded/replayed identity reaches a directory operation
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Bound parsing/session/work; verify channel/authentication/authorization before mutation; no credential success from transport alone.
boundaries.residual_risk: The existing RootDSE parser is only a small lab subset; future protocol implementations need their own client/fault proof.

boundaries.title: Core authorization and management mutation
misuse_cases: Caller substitutes target/scope or a stale grant
Management path marks itself a privileged replicator
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: One core evaluator and typed operation boundary, current target policy checks and durable audited writes; separate policy publication authority.
boundaries.residual_risk: Signed tickets and materialized inheritance/replica state can remain stale; expose the actual window.

boundaries.title: Core to transactional store/key custody
misuse_cases: Provider disappears or data/audit commit fails
SQL/error/diagnostic or ordinary attribute read leaks a secret
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Deny affected key operations, keep coupled local security/audit state durable, redact errors and separate secret custody from generic writers.
boundaries.residual_risk: A compromised DC process/root or lost custody is not repaired by memory safety; key rotation/clean recovery remain real operational gates.

boundaries.title: DC membership/replication and restore
misuse_cases: Unknown/revoked peer asks for credential changes
Reordered/partial batches or stale snapshot advance progress
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Authenticate/authorize exact peer/NC/secret scope, preserve metadata rules and reject unsafe epochs/progress before serving.
boundaries.residual_risk: A writable DC compromise is domain compromise; partitions cannot promise instantaneous global revocation.

boundaries.title: Browser/session to delegated API
misuse_cases: CSRF/XSS/session theft or recovery enrollment takeover
Self-approval or stale scope changes high-impact policy
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Phishing-resistant admin auth, CSRF/session controls, exact-scope expiry/step-up and denied browser/API/effective-access tests.
boundaries.residual_risk: Solo project review is not production separation of duties; web MFA does not impose MFA on every legacy domain protocol.

boundaries.title: Backup storage to clean restore
misuse_cases: Backup theft or insider deletion
Restore old keys/SYSVOL/epochs or require the failed domain to unlock its own recovery
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Protect independent encrypted/offline copies; verify coherent manifests and a clean-room restore/rotation before declaring recovery.
boundaries.residual_risk: No independent backup responder/custody or live recovery exercise is presently evidenced.

boundaries.title: Contributor/dependency/build to signing and consumer
misuse_cases: Untrusted PR/tool executes with signing authority
Wrong/replayed artifact is distributed as trusted
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Pinned inputs, scoped ephemeral CI, actual review, retained terms/SBOM and verified source/artifact/provenance; fail closed on audit services or evidence failure.
boundaries.residual_risk: Green scans cannot certify absent vulnerabilities or authenticate prose; independent production assessment remains required.

boundaries.title: IdP/CA/posture connector to identity
misuse_cases: Forged audience/nonce/template claim grants privilege
Connector URL becomes arbitrary privileged fetch
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Constrain issuers/destinations/claims and enrollment authority; provider loss/stale observations never become an automatic grant.
boundaries.residual_risk: Provider account compromise or stale third-party evidence is a distinct trust boundary, not cured by TLS.

boundaries.title: Device/relay/patch dispatcher
misuse_cases: Replay enrollment/inventory changes campaign targets
Poisoned relay/content or event storm starves authentication
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Unique revocable enrollment, authenticated timestamped inventory, immutable signed/expiring scoped jobs, native executors, quotas/canary pause and honest receipts.
boundaries.residual_risk: Endpoint root can defeat local enforcement; relays do not mint approvals and offline devices cannot honor immediate revocation.

boundaries.title: Operator/relay to remote session/file destination
misuse_cases: Consent/elevation or unattended-policy substitution
Traversal/symlink/overwrite race or upload autoexecution
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Separate session/elevation/recording/upload/execution grants; destination-at-open/finalization checks, staging/quotas and disconnect/rescue tests.
boundaries.residual_risk: Upload is not execution; recording/telemetry access and retention require privacy controls and supported-OS evidence.

boundaries.title: Sensor/rule/evidence to responder
misuse_cases: Forged/gapped events or PID reuse misidentify a target
False alerts or stolen response authority isolate the entire fleet
boundaries.required_denial_or_fault: Supported signed sensor/rule paths, visible gaps, exact typed expiring targets, mass-action limits/approval and independent rescue/emergency stop.
boundaries.residual_risk: A compromised kernel can defeat a sensor; detection is not unlimited execution authority or proof that prior compromise is undone.
